# ⬛ Checkers

**The jumping game.** Empty the board of enemy pieces — the lesson is trades and positioning.

## 🧠 Meaning

A capture is a trade; the player who controls the trade count wins.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Keep the back row intact.** Moving a back-row piece early exposes your rear — leave it until forced.
- **Trade when ahead.** Up one piece, every even exchange closes the game; down one piece, refuse all trades.
- **Force captures with a sacrifice.** Leave a piece as bait, then take two on the return jump.
- **Get to the kings row.** The first player to make kings has a runaway advantage — push the side of the board your opponent has abandoned.
- **Control the center.** Side pieces are boxed in; central pieces jump in four directions.
- **Watch the double jump.** Before any capture, count your opponent's landing square — a land in the middle often buys a follow-up jump.

## 🎲 Played

# ♟️ Chess

**The strategy game.** Control the center and convert — the lesson is pattern memory and calculation.

## 🧠 Meaning

Every move is a question about the board; the grind is seeing one move deeper each time.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Control the center.** Occupy or pressure e4/d4/e5/d5; a pawn in the middle outposts your pieces.
- **Develop before attacking.** Knights out, bishops out, castle early. Pieces on their first rank defend nothing.
- **Every move has a purpose.** Don't push pawns that don't fight for space or open lines.
- **Don't grab free pawns blindly.** Queens and rooks in the open get hunted — count attackers and defenders first.
- **Trade when ahead, simplify when winning.** Fewer pieces makes a material lead decisive.
- **Endgame shortcut: opposition and the rook.** In king-pawn endgames, shoulder the enemy king; rook endgames want the rook behind the passed pawn.
- **Tempo is a resource.** A check that forces a move gives you two moves in a row — use it to win the race.

## 🎲 Played

# 🔴 Connect 4

**The drop game.** Line up four first — the lesson is threat reading and zugzwang.

## 🧠 Meaning

The board is decided by threats, not moves; whoever forces a pattern wins.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Take the center column.** It's in every diagonal and horizontal — the only spot that can threaten from the first move.
- **Create double threats.** A move that sets up two winning lines at once is unstoppable — your opponent can block only one.
- **Block, then extend.** After blocking, always check if your blocking piece itself creates a new threat.
- **Force the opponent to fill columns.** If you can make the third move in a column, the fourth is yours or a threat.
- **Zugzwang is the win.** When every column is bad for the opponent, their forced move opens your win — play to exhaust their safe columns.
- **Mirror the center early.** Don't let the opponent own the middle; respond in the center column immediately.

## 🎲 Played

# 🁢 Dominoes

**The blocking game.** Empty your hand and read the table — the lesson is counting and control.

## 🧠 Meaning

Whoever controls the open ends controls the game; counting tiles turns luck into math.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Count the pips.** Track every tile played and the numbers remaining in hand; the open ends are the whole game.
- **Feed the suit you hold.** Play the number you still carry tiles for, so you never get stuck without a match.
- **Block the heavy suit.** If the opponent is holding doubles of a number, keep that suit closed on the table.
- **Empty your high tiles first.** The double-six is dead weight at the end — shed it while the table is open.
- **Force the draw.** If your play leaves the opponent unmatched, they pay — pick plays that close their options.
- **Endgame: keep one of each.** Holding both open numbers late means you always have a move; the opponent stalls first.

# 🕵️ Guess Who?

**Cara a Cara.** The investigation game — ask questions to eliminate faces until only theirs remains.

## 🧠 Meaning

The game is information gathering. Every question should cut the remaining faces roughly in half.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Split the board, not the people.** Ask about the most common feature first — hair color, glasses, facial hair — so the largest group flips down.
- **Always binary search.** After each answer, the field should shrink by ~50%; if a question only removes two faces, it was wasted.
- **Ask about big categories early.** "Does your person have glasses?" is often better than "Is your person Sam?" — never guess a name until the field is tiny.
- **Ride the biggest flip.** If a question answers your way, follow with the next most common feature in that surviving group.
- **Keep a mental shortlist.** Track the faces still standing; guess only when you have one or two left.

## 🎲 Played

# 🗼 Jenga

**The stacking game.** Pull blocks and keep the tower standing — the lesson is steady hands and nerve.

## 🧠 Meaning

The tower falls for the player who rushes. Slow wins.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Pull from the middle rows.** Mid-tower bricks are loosest and least risky to free.
- **Never the top finished row.** Completed rows settle — disturb them last.
- **Steady two-finger pull.** Flick it out with a fast clean motion; hesitation wobbles the whole stack.
- **Watch the loose brick.** If a brick visibly sticks out, it comes out easily — but check it's not load-bearing first.
- **Don't let the tower lean.** Push back gently toward the side you haven't weakened; a straight tower survives longer.
- **Patience is the weapon.** Let the opponent play faster; their mistakes are your win.

## 🎲 Played

# 🏢 Monopoly

**The money game.** Buy, build, and bleed opponents dry — the lesson is cash management under pressure.

## 🧠 Meaning

Ownership is a machine; houses are the throttle. Never let the machine stall for lack of rent.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Buy orange and red first.** Most landed-on squares of the board; the orange set is the highest-value cheap purchase.
- **Houses over hotels.** Three houses on a set earn more than one hotel for the same cash; build wide before building tall.
- **Never break your cash reserve.** Keep enough to pay rent; bankrupting yourself on a single roll is the real loss.
- **Trade to complete sets.** Two useless properties are worth one complete set to someone else — swap for the third piece.
- **Jail is a parking lot.** Mid-game, staying in jail avoids the expensive tail of the board — don't rush to pay bail.
- **Count the doubles.** You roll out of jail on a double; know when the exit is forced and which squares that exposes.

## 🎲 Played

# 🃏 UNO

**The shedding game.** Empty your hand first — the lesson is card counting and timing.

## 🧠 Meaning

The player who burns their hand fastest wins; hold the control cards for the right moment.

## 🗝️ Beat it with ease

- **Count the colors.** Track roughly how many cards each player plays per color; lead into the color they lack.
- **Hold skips and reverses.** They end the turn of the player about to win — don't waste them early.
- **Save the wild +4 for the kill.** When an opponent has one card left, the +4 is a win button — never spend it on a boring turn.
- **Keep a matching color.** Against a +2, always hold at least one card in a color you can play so you don't draw.
- **Go out on +cards.** A +2 or +4 as your final card stops the next player — the perfect finisher.
- **Draw the deck, not your opponent.** When stuck, match the pile color you already hold the most of.

# ⚔️ Pokémon

## 🧠 Meaning

Catch, build, battle — the team and the competition are the point, not the checklist. Competing against strong teams is the endless pursuit; the grind (dex tail, brute-force shiny) is the trap.

> 🚪 **Retired from Nintendo from the Wii U era onward** — titles marked 🔒 **launched after** the Wii era and were not played. Story done through Gen IV, dex ~80%.

## 🎮 Mainline games

**Why to play:** the region-journey lane — catch, train, gyms, League; player canon, not Ash canon.

## 📓 Retrospective

Notes from the runs — what worked, what to drop.

table: | All-HM adventure team — navigate the whole game without swapping mid-run | Full-dex completion (the 80→100% tail ate all your time) |
| Balanced type coverage + swap-to-weakness — beat any gym without a roster swap | Fishing / pokedex hunting as a grind — repetition with no luck |
| Items only as emergency (revive), Elite League with no items | Contests and berry customization — never clicked |
| Breeding / Ditto — IV propagation curiosity | Competition that gets easy once the team is strong (repetitive) |
| Team-building against strong opponents — the infinite pursuit | Pure-random shiny script — 4k+ run/repeat, easy to miss the target |
| Shiny hunting — awesome, but needs a method, not brute force | |

## 🧠 What the games taught

- **Type chart** — super effective (2×), not very effective (0.5×), immunities (0×). The whole fight loop is **swap to the weakness** while managing resources.
- **HM coverage** — a team built to carry the required moves navigates the entire game; no mid-run swaps needed.
- **EVs** — effort values summarize what a Pokémon actually experienced in battle; training focus shapes stats.
- **Resource discipline** — items are an emergency lane, not a crutch; the no-item Elite League is the real test.

## 🥚 Breeding

**Ditto** breeds with almost any egg group — eggs inherit an IV spread from the parents, so Ditto plus a good partner propagates stats. Perfect IVs are the competitive breeding target.

## ✨ Shiny hunting

Different palette, very rare — ~1/8192 in Gen III–IV wild encounters; **Masuda method** improves the odds via breeding. The fun is real, but pure random encounter + run repeats 4k+ times and is easy
to miss the target — use a method next time.
